samples.question: This canvas carries a single rotor. The rotor is a ring of exactly eight small coloured squares, evenly spaced around a common centre, one square each in red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple and pink. These eight positions are the stations of the ring. Just outside the ring, opposite exactly one station, there is a solid black curved bracket: that bracket is the read window and it never moves. Inside the ring, at the hub, there is a stack of solid black turn glyphs, one turn per line. A line consists of a black triangle followed by one, two or three small black square pips. The pips say how many stations that turn advances the ring. The triangle says which way: a triangle whose point aims to the right turns the whole ring of coloured squares one station at a time in the clockwise direction, and a triangle whose point aims to the left turns it in the anticlockwise direction. The turns are applied in order from the top line of the hub stack to the bottom line, starting from the ring exactly as it is printed. The ring is a closed loop, so a square that passes the last station carries on round to the next one. The whole ring turns together, so the eight colours keep their cyclic order; only the window is fixed. Placement and tilt of the rotor vary freely from picture to picture; every faint grey mark beyond it belongs to the backdrop and means nothing. After all of the turns in the hub stack have been carried out, which coloured square is standing at the read window? Answer with one of red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple or pink.
